builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
summary: ARCHER replaces free-form chain-of-thought imitation with supervised typed action traces (reasoning steps, calculator calls, runtime observations, verification actions) followed by asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning with gated trajectory rewards. The cost is a two-stage training pipeline: rationale-to-trace compilation, a deterministic calculator runtime, and multi-component RL reward infrastructure, plus the engineering burden of maintaining the execution environment. It can fail when compiled traces are noisy or unrepresentative of the target tasks, when the gated rewards are miscalibrated, or when deployed without the same runtime assumptions used during training, and the absolute AIME accuracies of sub-10B models may remain too low for production reliance.
rationale: The method requires a full custom two-stage training and RL reward pipeline across multiple backbones, which exceeds a 24 GB GPU and limited budget, so the reader should track it rather than adopt it, while still borrowing the design pattern of calculator-grounded verification via prompting or API-based tool use.
technique: Executable action-trace training with hierarchical RL

claims.statement: ARCHER replaces free-form chain-of-thought imitation with supervised typed action traces (reasoning steps, calculator calls, runtime observations, verification actions) followed by asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning with gated trajectory rewards. The cost is a two-stage training pipeline: rationale-to-trace compilation, a deterministic calculator runtime, and multi-component RL reward infrastructure, plus the engineering burden of maintaining the execution environment. It can fail when compiled traces are noisy or unrepresentative of the target tasks, when the gated rewards are miscalibrated, or when deployed without the same runtime assumptions used during training, and the absolute AIME accuracies of sub-10B models may remain too low for production reliance.

Improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points macro-average across benchmarks, including +8.95 points on MATH-500 and +5.33/+5.34 points on AIME-2024/2025, across five sub-10B backbones.
